svg.text: DigitLab / clean accuracy is not bounded-input robustness
Real UCI 8-by-8 digits. Official writer-independent test split, not a random pool of test images.
1 Fixed training/validation choices, then a frozen-test audit
2 Every number below is correct / 1797, not a robustness certificate
L-infinity radius uses normalized pixels [0,1]; epsilon 0.1 means 1.6 original pixel-count units.
PGD: 20 steps, 3 random starts; pool includes clean, FGSM, starts and every iterate.
All pixels clipped to [0,1] and projected to the radius. One fixed random-sign draw, no tuning.
3 Selected examples: first three successes, then first three survivors
MLP PGD at epsilon 0.1. These display choices are not a representative sample. No imperceptibility claim.
4 Transfer is a different question from an adaptive attack
1NN correct on MLP PGD images: epsilon0.1
These are MLP-targeted images, not attacks optimized against 1NN. Do not rank robust models from this.
Digits: Alpaydin & Kaynak (1998), UCI, DOI 10.24432/C50P49, CC BY 4.0; attack images are adaptations.
Small historical benchmark, fixed protocol and seed. Not MNIST, production OCR, SOTA or certified robustness.
